review: Independent freeze review of the second two-arm companion attempt (gate C5 only), before any paid call. Read-only: no paid model call, no API key read, no pytest, no service or database started, nothing pushed; the only file written in the clone is this one. No held-out content was read: the scenario and findings files of this attempt were only hashed, counted (wc, grep -c of fixed patterns, never displayed) and passed to c5-precheck.py, freeze.py and novelty.py, which print counts and codes only. In the earlier attempt's private root only control/*.json was read.

findings.what: The new hard-moment definition repeats the C5 author brief's own wording for the item it is tested by. The product's server instructions now define a hard shared moment as 'a hard time you got through together (a bad night you sat with them through, or the user upset with you)' (src/membrain/host.py, the only product change between ef0e8727 and 3afc0dda). The code comment says the change was made because the first two-arm attempt's host left unsaved 'a bad night the user said they had got through together': that is, after a spent held-out scenario failed on this item. The C5 author brief has told every author since 4175ba28 (2026-11-16, before the product change) to write the hard moment as 'a bad night the companion helped the user through' (c5-author-brief.md item 10). The hard-moment probe used the same situation (six bad nights, three reconciliations). The binding reports the probe's 9 of 9 and the possible eagerness. It does not say that the product's example names the very situation the scenario authors are told to write.
findings.where: maturity-c5-execution-2026-11-17c.md, second comparability table (Runtime row) and 'Limits a C5 result will have' (the hard-moment bullet); src/membrain/host.py; evaluations/acceptance-kit/c5-author-brief.md lines 218-219
findings.why_it_matters: On this attempt the shared_moments hard case mostly tests whether the host follows an instruction that already names the scenario's situation. It does not test whether the product generalises to other hard moments. A pass on that item is weak evidence for the claim 'the companion layers hold on held-out lives'. The record must say so, whatever the result. The run itself is not affected, so this does not block spending.

findings.what: The time bound on a retried host call is overstated, and one clause is wrong. Decision 6 says clock_already_past can take 'several fully failed retried host calls in one session'. But a host call whose three sends all fail ends the arm. Only a call with at most two interrupted sends survives: up to 2 x 600 s + 30 + 120 s plus the third send's own duration. The 600 s client timeout limits silence, not a send. The provider documents keep-alive empty lines on non-streaming requests, and c5-harness.md itself says 'longer if a response trickles in'. So 'up to about 33 minutes per host call' (Limits, and the second comparability table) is typical, not a bound.
findings.where: maturity-c5-execution-2026-11-17c.md decision 6 (clock_already_past bullet), second comparability table (Provider failures row), Limits (first bullet); c5-harness.py Host.call
findings.why_it_matters: This only affects how a reader judges the scenario-clock risk in P. Validity reports the actual delay per session, and clock_already_past still guards the gap. So nothing is mis-scored, but the record should cite measured delays, not the 33-minute figure.

findings.what: The kit's novelty check misses public material that overlaps most. novelty.py's public set is top-level evaluations/*scenario*.py plus evidence/**/scenario_*.py.gz. It does not see the first two-arm attempt's spent scenarios (published only inside evidence/maturity-c5-attempt-stop-2026-11-17/attempt-evidence.tar.gz) or the public C5 authoring diagnostics d1 to d3. Those are the files of the same items under the same templates. I reproduced the public figures (C1 0.08%, C2 0.11%, 21 files). The overlaps that matter (C1 6.24% with spent c1 and 5.74% with d2; C2 4.96% with spent c2 and 4.47% with d3) come only from the operator's wrapper. The binding reports both sets honestly. Its explanation (the criteria templates fix the coverage cases' wording) is plausible, because the public diagnostics written to the same templates give similar figures, but it was not verified.
findings.why_it_matters: Every figure is well within the 10% threshold, and the authors never saw those files, so this attempt is not affected. A future attempt that relies on the kit alone would understate overlap with published same-item scenarios.

Retry rule in code, matching the binding. Interrupted are the ten transport classes (ConnectTimeout, ReadTimeout, WriteTimeout, PoolTimeout, TimeoutException, ConnectError, ReadError, WriteError, CloseError, RemoteProtocolError) when no final status was received, HTTP 429/500/502/503/504, and a complete 2xx body that is blank, not JSON, or JSON without usage. Each is settled at its bound with the ledger left open (ProviderInterrupted). Fatal: any other status, settled-usage problems, unknown classes, SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt, and a transport error after a final 4xx. Host.call resends the identical body after 30 s and then 120 s, three sends at most, each counted against the cap of turns*5. The third interruption, or a cap with no send left, makes the harness call guard.stop(kind) and raise. Each interrupted send is written and fsynced to provider-interruptions.jsonl (format 2) before the wait. The SIGTERM handler blocks the ledger unless the lock is held. A signal during a retry wait therefore blocks the ledger and exits, and validity would refuse that unretried line, but the run has stopped anyway.

Driver wiring: in live mode the driver refuses --runner and --validity, so default validity and the ledger (from C5_BILLING_LEDGER) are always used. It records ledger_seq_before before each scenario and runs acceptance_review.py ledger-check --after-seq after a passing validity. That check compares (code, request_bytes) multisets between the ledger's interrupted entries and both run directories' lines, and a non-zero exit makes the scenario invalid. Validity refuses a malformed interruption file and an unretried interruption.

Supervisor and stop chain: c5-run-scenario.sh runs P, then its cleanup and port check, then F. On TERM or a failed arm it runs c5-harness.py --stop before killing the arms. limitations: One host model (deepseek-v4-pro, thinking enabled, max_tokens 16,384) through the harness's emulation, not Claude Code or any real host. One seeded type (intj). Two scenarios. Each of the 13 items has one case (two for the mood) in one language mix only. A pass or fail may rest on one or two judgements.

Each scenario's wording rests on one Sonnet review of 54 s or 70 s, with no verification round and its 2 minor findings unapplied. The criteria templates fix every coverage case's 'must' and 'must not', so a template that tests the wrong thing errs the same way in every case of its item.

The shared_moments hard case is tested against a server instruction whose example is the brief's own situation, written after a spent scenario failed that item (major finding). The wider definition may also be eager, and that is unmeasured.

The retry has never met a real interruption: it has been tested with a fake transport only. A retried reply is scored like any other, and its delay moves P's scenario clock, which F does not have. The bound rests on two assumptions: no more prompt tokens than bytes (checked against the published tokenizer), and max_tokens capping reasoning tokens (implied, not stated). If the second is false, up to 10.17 CNY per interrupted send is uncounted.
P sends reasoning_content back only within a turn's rounds. If the provider enforces its rule, the attempt stops early with a 400, the request's whole reservation kept on the guard's count.
Partial blinding with two arms: memory remarks can reveal the arm, and the remark count undercounts.

F has no memory layers. It learns page-only settings from one fixed line and is told about resets while P's host is not, which tilts reset cases toward F. F's critical errors bound P's host-caused allowance.
Host labelling decides type 6. A fail caused by a host step still counts as a fail: the result is for memBrain together with this host under emulation.
A not_applicable page action, or a host that never makes the expected call, leaves its item unexercised while the gate can still pass. c1 has 1 page action and c2 has 3.
No off-the-record stretch: pause on the user's words, resume and honesty about an unrecorded stretch are not exercised.

R4 passed on runtime a85ca152. host.py and persona_tool.py changed substantially since (436 lines in 6 src files), so the R4 result and a C5 result on 3afc0dda do not qualify one release runtime together.

The guard count is conservative: the real bill was about a sixth to a third of it. But the guard count is what can stop the run, and nothing bounds the cost estimate above. c2 runs after c1 with no decision point.
